name: Storybloq/storybloq

hlido_opinion.headline: A local harness that keeps Claude Code and Codex context in a git-tracked .story/ directory — the ownership model is the pitch, and it is a credible one.
hlido_opinion.body: Storybloq addresses the failure every heavy coding-agent user knows: the next session starts cold. Its answer is to write the project's working memory to plain files in a .story/ directory beside the source — tickets, issues, lessons and handovers — tracked by git, readable and editable by a human or any AI. A handover is given real structure: what changed and which checks ran, why it changed and the reasoning behind the decisions, and what comes next including open questions and blockers. Around that sit a CLI, an MCP server the vendor says exposes 53 tools callable directly by Claude Code and Codex without subprocess spawning, a /story skill, and a Mac app. The ownership claim is the part that matters commercially: the CLI and MCP server run locally, so there is no Storybloq cloud subscription, no hosted-MCP quota and no network round trip to read your own project record. It also handles multi-repo work, showing how stories connect across web, API and mobile while each repo keeps its own history, and a "Duet" mode coordinates a manager agent that scopes work and checks evidence against workers. Confidence here is low, and deliberately so. Hlido read the marketing surface only; no install was performed, so the 53-tool MCP server, the handover quality and the multi-repo view are all unverified. Our automated checks were unusually weak on this page: no CTA was resolved despite a visible install command, no pricing or access tier was found, and no demo was reachable — the page leads with an npm command rather than a conventional signup path, which is honest for a local tool but leaves a buyer with little to evaluate.

tier_rationale: STEADY (70) for a well-specified local-first harness whose core idea — agent context as git-tracked plain files you own — is sound and clearly explained, with a documented CLI, MCP server and Mac app. Held at low confidence because nothing was installed and the automated surface checks resolved no CTA, pricing or demo.
what_it_does_well: Keeps agent working memory as plain files in .story/ beside the source, tracked by git and editable by both humans and agents
Gives handovers real structure — what changed and checks run, why it changed and the reasoning, what comes next with open questions and blockers
Runs the CLI and MCP server locally, so there is no cloud subscription, no hosted-MCP quota and no network round trip to read your own project record
Covers multi-repo work, connecting stories across web, API and mobile while each repo keeps its own history
Offers a manager-and-worker Duet mode where the manager scopes work and checks evidence, with assignments and approvals stored with the project
what_it_fails_at: The vendor's 53-tool MCP server, handover quality and multi-repo view are all unverified — nothing was installed in this review
Automated checks resolved no CTA, no pricing or access tier and no reachable demo, so a buyer has very little to evaluate before installing
Scoped to Claude Code and Codex, so value depends on already standardising on those harnesses
Adopting it means adding a convention (.story/ plus a schema of tickets, issues, lessons, handovers) that the whole team has to maintain for the record to stay honest
best_for: Heavy Claude Code or Codex users who repeatedly lose context between sessions and want the record in their own repo
Teams coordinating several coding agents across multiple repositories who need assignments and approvals stored with the code
Engineers who refuse hosted agent-memory services and want plain, inspectable, git-versioned files
not_recommended_for: Occasional coding-agent users for whom a per-project file convention is more overhead than the problem it solves
Teams on other harnesses, where the Claude Code and Codex focus leaves most of the value unreachable
Buyers who need published pricing and a working demo before installing anything
red_flags: A specific, impressive capability number — 53 MCP tools — is asserted on a page with no demo and no documented tool list reachable without installing, so the claim cannot be checked before adoption

compared_to.verdict_diff: Mem0 is a general memory layer an agent calls at runtime; Storybloq is a project-scoped workflow record in git with tickets, handovers and approvals. Mem0 for recall across sessions, Storybloq when the team also needs to review and direct the work.
compared_to.preferred_for_axis: generic memory recall vs project workflow record

compared_to.verdict_diff: Both keep agent context in local inspectable files; SwarmVault compiles a knowledge graph from sources, Storybloq tracks the project's live workflow — stories, issues, handovers. Pick by whether you need knowledge or coordination.

evidence_urls.claim: Stories, issues, lessons and handovers live as plain files in a .story/ directory beside the source, versioned with git and editable by hand
The CLI and MCP server run locally, with no Storybloq cloud subscription, hosted-MCP quota or network round trip required to access the project record
Installed via npm install -g @storybloq/storybloq@latest with storybloq setup --client all, positioned as a harness for Claude Code and Codex
An MCP server exposing 53 tools callable directly by Claude Code and Codex without subprocess spawning (vendor-stated; not verified by Hlido)
Automated public-surface checks resolved no CTA, no pricing or access tier and no reachable demo on the captured page

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Claude Code and Codex call the local MCP server directly (the vendor states 53 tools, no subprocess spawning) and a /story skill exposes the same workflow in-session. The agent reads and writes the .story/ directory, so the next session resumes from the recorded handover rather than from nothing.

summary: A local harness that keeps Claude Code and Codex context in a git-tracked .story/ directory — the ownership model is the pitch, and it is a credible one.
